---
title: "Raw Milk Survey Analysis - 01: Data Cleaning"
output: html_document
---

Imports the raw Qualtrics export, applies eligibility filters, builds the
analysis-ready variables, and writes the cleaned datasets that 02/03/04 read.
Any change made here carries through to all three outcome scripts the next
time they are knit.

Outputs:

- `cleaned_survey_data.csv` (from `survey_grouped`) -- main analysis dataset
- `survey_base_data.csv` (from `survey_base`) -- filtered but pre-grouping; used by 03

**Set the working directory (or use an RStudio Project) to the folder
containing `survey_results.csv` before knitting.**

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)   # dplyr, ggplot2, readr, stringr, forcats, tibble
library(janitor)
library(scales)
library(gt)
library(broom)
```

## 1. Import

Qualtrics exports two header rows: row 1 holds the question names, row 2 holds
the ImportId metadata. Read the names from row 1, then skip both.

```{r import}
survey_raw      <- read_csv("survey_results.csv", col_names = FALSE)
new_names       <- as.character(survey_raw[1, ])
survey_results  <- read_csv("survey_results.csv", skip = 2, col_names = FALSE)
colnames(survey_results) <- new_names

survey_results <- survey_results %>%
  clean_names() %>%
  rename(
    age                          = q9,
    state                        = q11,
    milk_consumed                = q1,
    raw_milk_heating             = q2,
    info_source                  = q3,
    raw_milk_consumers_household = q4,
    raw_milk_taste               = q5,
    raw_milk_nutrition           = q6,
    raw_milk_sickness            = q7,
    milk_safety_concern          = q8,
    sex_at_birth                 = q10,
    education                    = q12,
    political_affiliation        = q13
  )
```

## 2. Eligibility filter

Three exclusions: under 18 / declined age, non-US / declined state, and the
leftover Qualtrics metadata row. Sex at birth is NOT an exclusion criterion.
Result: N = 1,075 eligible.

```{r filter}
survey_base <- survey_results %>%
  filter(
    !age   %in% c("Under 18", "Prefer not to answer"),
    !state %in% c("I don’t live in the USA", "Prefer not to answer"),
    milk_consumed != '{"ImportId":"QID1"}'
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # Outcome 1: any raw milk consumption. NA for "Neither" and "Prefer not to
    # answer" -- these are the 177 dropped to reach the N = 898 analytic sample.
    raw_milk_binary = case_when(
      milk_consumed %in% c("Raw dairy milk", "Both raw and pasteurized dairy milk") ~ 1,
      milk_consumed == "Pasteurized dairy milk" ~ 0,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),
    # Outcome 3: consistent at-home thermal treatment (Q2, raw consumers only)
    heating_binary = case_when(
      raw_milk_heating %in% c("More than half the time", "Always") ~ 1,
      raw_milk_heating %in% c("Never", "Less than half the time",
                              "Approximately half the time") ~ 0,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  )
```

## 3. Derived variables

Notes on two recodes that have bitten before:

- Education uses `startsWith("Post-graduate")` because the raw string contains a
  curly apostrophe ("Master's") that breaks exact matching. High school
  graduates / GED belong in "High school or less".
- Household risk matches `"limited immunity"`, not `"Immunocompromised"` -- the
  survey text is "People with limited immunity (e.g., getting chemotherapy)".
  At-risk categories are checked first, so a respondent selecting both an
  at-risk group and "None of the above" resolves to "Has at-risk member".

`taste_grouped` / `nutrition_belief_group` send "I don't know" and "Prefer not
to answer" to NA (3 levels). `taste_grouped2` / `nutrition_grouped2` keep them
as a category (4 levels). Both are used downstream: the 4-level versions in the
R_Any and R_Exclusive models, the 3-level versions in the thermal crosstabs.

```{r derive}
survey_grouped <- survey_base %>%
  mutate(
    # Sex: "Other [specify]" and "Prefer not to answer" -> NA
    sex_at_birth = if_else(sex_at_birth %in% c("Male", "Female"),
                           sex_at_birth, NA_character_),

    age_grouped = case_when(
      age == "18-24" ~ "18–24",
      age == "25-34" ~ "25–34",
      age == "35-44" ~ "35–44",
      age == "45-54" ~ "45–54",
      age %in% c("55-64", "65 or over") ~ "55+",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    education_grouped = case_when(
      education %in% c("Below high school", "Some high school",
                       "High school graduate (grade 12 or GED certificate)") ~ "High school or less",
      education %in% c("Technical, trade, or vocational school after high school",
                       "Some college or 2 year Associate Degree") ~ "Some college or technical",
      education == "College graduate (BS, BA, or other 4-year degree)" ~ "College graduate",
      startsWith(education, "Post-graduate") ~ "Graduate or professional",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    region = case_when(
      state %in% c("Connecticut","Maine","Massachusetts","New Hampshire","Rhode Island",
                   "Vermont","New Jersey","New York","Pennsylvania") ~ "Northeast",
      state %in% c("Illinois","Indiana","Michigan","Ohio","Wisconsin","Iowa","Kansas",
                   "Minnesota","Missouri","Nebraska","North Dakota","South Dakota") ~ "Midwest",
      state %in% c("Delaware","Florida","Georgia","Maryland","North Carolina",
                   "South Carolina","Virginia","District of Columbia","West Virginia",
                   "Alabama","Kentucky","Mississippi","Tennessee","Arkansas","Louisiana",
                   "Oklahoma","Texas") ~ "South",
      state %in% c("Arizona","Colorado","Idaho","Montana","Nevada","New Mexico","Utah",
                   "Wyoming","Alaska","California","Hawaii","Oregon","Washington") ~ "West",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    # Leaners folded into the party they lean toward
    politics_grouped = case_when(
      political_affiliation %in% c("Strong Democrat", "Not very strong Democrat",
                                   "Independent, close to Democrat") ~ "Democrat",
      political_affiliation %in% c("Strong Republican", "Not very strong Republican",
                                   "Independent, close to Republican") ~ "Republican",
      political_affiliation %in% c("Independent, close to neither",
                                   "Other party affiliation [specify]") ~ "Independent/Other",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    # 3-level: non-definitive answers -> NA
    taste_grouped = case_when(
      raw_milk_taste == "Raw is better"         ~ "Raw better",
      raw_milk_taste == "Pasteurized is better" ~ "Pasteurized better",
      raw_milk_taste == "They are equal"        ~ "Equal",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    nutrition_belief_group = case_when(
      raw_milk_nutrition == "Raw is better"         ~ "Raw better",
      raw_milk_nutrition == "Pasteurized is better" ~ "Pasteurized better",
      raw_milk_nutrition == "They are equal"        ~ "Equal",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    # 4-level: non-definitive answers retained as a category
    taste_grouped2 = case_when(
      raw_milk_taste == "Raw is better"         ~ "Raw better",
      raw_milk_taste == "Pasteurized is better" ~ "Pasteurized better",
      raw_milk_taste == "They are equal"        ~ "Equal",
      TRUE ~ "Missing"
    ),
    nutrition_grouped2 = case_when(
      raw_milk_nutrition == "Raw is better"         ~ "Raw better",
      raw_milk_nutrition == "Pasteurized is better" ~ "Pasteurized better",
      raw_milk_nutrition == "They are equal"        ~ "Equal",
      TRUE ~ "Missing"
    ),

    household_risk_group = case_when(
      grepl("Children aged 5 or younger", raw_milk_consumers_household) |
      grepl("Adults aged 65 or older",    raw_milk_consumers_household) |
      grepl("limited immunity",           raw_milk_consumers_household) |
      grepl("Pregnant",                   raw_milk_consumers_household) ~ "Has at-risk member",
      grepl("None of the above", raw_milk_consumers_household) ~ "No at-risk member",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )
```

## 4. Sample reconciliation

```{r reconcile}
elig_trace <- tibble(
  step = c("Raw export (incl. metadata row)",
           "After removing under 18 / declined age",
           "After removing non-US / declined state and metadata row",
           "After removing milk non-response (analytic sample)"),
  n = c(
    nrow(survey_results),
    survey_results %>%
      filter(!age %in% c("Under 18", "Prefer not to answer")) %>% nrow(),
    nrow(survey_grouped),
    sum(!is.na(survey_grouped$raw_milk_binary))
  )
)
print(elig_trace)

cat("\nMilk consumption (eligible sample):\n")
print(table(survey_grouped$milk_consumed, useNA = "ifany"))

cat("\nHousehold risk group:\n")
print(table(survey_grouped$household_risk_group, useNA = "ifany"))

cat("\nSex at birth in analytic sample (3 NAs retained; not an exclusion):\n")
print(survey_grouped %>% filter(!is.na(raw_milk_binary)) %>% count(sex_at_birth))

stopifnot(nrow(survey_grouped) == 1075,
          sum(!is.na(survey_grouped$raw_milk_binary)) == 898)
cat("\nVERIFIED: 1,075 eligible; 898 analytic sample.\n")
```

## 5. Raw response distributions

Every response option as offered, before any recoding. Only Q5-Q8 included an
"I don't know" option; all other questions offered "Prefer not to answer" only.

```{r raw-distributions}
raw_vars <- c(
  milk_consumed         = "Milk consumption (Q1)",
  raw_milk_heating      = "Heating frequency (Q2)",
  info_source           = "Trusted information source (Q3)",
  raw_milk_taste        = "Perceived taste (Q5)",
  raw_milk_nutrition    = "Nutrition beliefs (Q6)",
  raw_milk_sickness     = "Perceived illness risk (Q7)",
  milk_safety_concern   = "H5N1 safety concern (Q8)",
  age                   = "Age (Q9)",
  sex_at_birth          = "Sex at birth (Q10)",
  education             = "Education (Q12)",
  political_affiliation = "Political orientation (Q13)"
)

for (v in names(raw_vars)) {
  cat("\n=====", raw_vars[[v]], "=====\n")
  tb  <- table(survey_grouped[[v]], useNA = "ifany")
  out <- data.frame(Response = names(tb), n = as.integer(tb),
                    pct = round(100 * as.integer(tb) / nrow(survey_grouped), 1))
  out$Response[is.na(out$Response)] <- "<NA>"
  print(out[order(-out$n), ], row.names = FALSE)
}
```

Q4 is select-all-that-apply, so each option is counted separately.

```{r q4-options}
q4_options <- c("Children aged 5 or younger", "Adults aged 65 or older",
                "People with limited immunity", "Pregnant individuals",
                "None of the above", "Prefer not to answer")

tibble(
  Option = q4_options,
  n = sapply(q4_options, function(o)
        sum(str_detect(survey_grouped$raw_milk_consumers_household, fixed(o)), na.rm = TRUE))
) %>%
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / nrow(survey_grouped), 1)) %>%
  print()

cat("\nOptions selected per respondent:\n")
print(table(sapply(survey_grouped$raw_milk_consumers_household,
                   function(x) sum(str_detect(x, fixed(q4_options))))))
```

## 6. Descriptive tables

```{r descriptives}
summarize_categorical <- function(df, var_name) {
  df %>%
    group_by(!!sym(var_name)) %>%
    summarise(Number = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(Percent = Number / sum(Number) * 100) %>%
    rename(Level = !!sym(var_name)) %>%
    mutate(Variable = var_name) %>%
    select(Variable, Level, Number, Percent)
}

descriptive_vars <- c(
  age_grouped            = "Age group",
  sex_at_birth           = "Sex at birth",
  region                 = "Region",
  household_risk_group   = "Cohabitation with high-risk raw milk consumer",
  taste_grouped2         = "Perceived taste (Q5)",
  nutrition_grouped2     = "Nutrition beliefs (Q6)",
  raw_milk_sickness      = "Perceived illness risk (Q7)",
  milk_safety_concern    = "H5N1 safety concern (Q8)",
  info_source            = "Trusted information source (Q3)",
  education_grouped      = "Education level (Q12)",
  politics_grouped       = "Political orientation (Q13)",
  milk_consumed          = "Milk consumption (Q1)",
  raw_milk_heating       = "Heating frequency (Q2)"
)

summary_table <- bind_rows(
  lapply(names(descriptive_vars), summarize_categorical, df = survey_grouped)
) %>%
  mutate(Variable = recode(Variable, !!!as.list(descriptive_vars)))

write_csv(summary_table, "Survey_Summary_Statistics.csv")

summary_table %>%
  group_by(Variable) %>%
  mutate(Variable = ifelse(row_number() == 1, Variable, "")) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(title = "Descriptive Statistics",
             subtitle = paste0("Eligible sample (N = ", nrow(survey_grouped), ")")) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = Percent, decimals = 1) %>%
  cols_align(align = "center", columns = c(Number, Percent)) %>%
  tab_options(table.font.size = px(12), data_row.padding = px(2),
              heading.align = "left", table.width = pct(90))
```

Household risk subgroups. Indented categories are not mutually exclusive.

```{r household-risk-table}
at_risk_breakdown <- tibble(
  `Household Member Category` = c(
    "Any at-risk household member",
    "  Children aged 5 or younger",
    "  Adults aged 65 or older",
    "  People with limited immunity (e.g., getting chemotherapy)",
    "  Pregnant individuals",
    "No at-risk member",
    "Prefer not to answer (unclassified)"
  ),
  N = c(
    sum(survey_grouped$household_risk_group == "Has at-risk member", na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(str_detect(survey_grouped$raw_milk_consumers_household, fixed("Children aged 5 or younger")), na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(str_detect(survey_grouped$raw_milk_consumers_household, fixed("Adults aged 65 or older")), na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(str_detect(survey_grouped$raw_milk_consumers_household, fixed("People with limited immunity")), na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(str_detect(survey_grouped$raw_milk_consumers_household, fixed("Pregnant individuals")), na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(survey_grouped$household_risk_group == "No at-risk member", na.rm = TRUE),
    sum(is.na(survey_grouped$household_risk_group))
  )
) %>%
  mutate(`% of Total Sample` = round(N / nrow(survey_grouped) * 100, 1))

write_csv(at_risk_breakdown, "Household_Risk_Breakdown.csv")

at_risk_breakdown %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(title = "Household Risk Group Breakdown",
             subtitle = paste0("Eligible sample (N = ", nrow(survey_grouped), ")")) %>%
  tab_style(style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
            locations = cells_body(rows = !startsWith(`Household Member Category`, "  "))) %>%
  tab_footnote(
    footnote = paste("Subgroups sum to more than 'Any at-risk household member'",
                     "because Q4 was select-all-that-apply."),
    locations = cells_column_labels(columns = `% of Total Sample`)) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = `% of Total Sample`, decimals = 1)
```

## 7. Free-text responses to "Other [specify]"

Used for the footnotes reporting what respondents wrote in. Reported for the
analytic sample (N = 898); change the filter to use the full eligible sample.

```{r free-text}
analytic <- survey_grouped %>% filter(!is.na(raw_milk_binary))

for (tv in c(q3_18_text = "Trusted information source (Q3)",
             q10_3_text = "Sex at birth (Q10)",
             q13_8_text = "Political orientation (Q13)") %>% names()) {
  if (!tv %in% names(analytic)) next
  vals <- analytic[[tv]]
  vals <- vals[!is.na(vals) & trimws(vals) != ""]
  cat("\n=====", tv, "-- free-text entries (n =", length(vals), ") =====\n")
  if (length(vals)) print(sort(table(vals), decreasing = TRUE))
}
```

## 8. Sensitivity: alternative education and political codings

Checks whether the grouping decisions in section 3 drive the results. Reported
in the manuscript as a sensitivity analysis; not used in any primary model.

```{r alt-codings}
alt <- survey_grouped %>%
  mutate(
    edu_4 = case_when(
      education %in% c("Below high school", "Some high school") |
        startsWith(education, "High school graduate") ~ "High school or less",
      startsWith(education, "Technical") |
        startsWith(education, "Some college")         ~ "Some college or technical",
      startsWith(education, "College graduate")       ~ "Bachelor's degree",
      startsWith(education, "Post-graduate")          ~ "Graduate or professional",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_),
    edu_3_top = case_when(
      edu_4 %in% c("Bachelor's degree", "Graduate or professional") ~ "Bachelor's or higher",
      TRUE ~ edu_4),
    edu_3_mid = case_when(
      edu_4 %in% c("Some college or technical", "Bachelor's degree") ~ "Some college to bachelor's",
      TRUE ~ edu_4),
    # Leaners counted as independents rather than partisans
    pol_leaners_ind = case_when(
      political_affiliation %in% c("Strong Democrat", "Not very strong Democrat") ~ "Democrat",
      political_affiliation %in% c("Strong Republican", "Not very strong Republican") ~ "Republican",
      startsWith(political_affiliation, "Independent") |
        startsWith(political_affiliation, "Other") ~ "Independent/Other",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_),
    pol_strong = case_when(
      political_affiliation == "Strong Democrat"   ~ "Strong Democrat",
      political_affiliation == "Strong Republican" ~ "Strong Republican",
      !is.na(political_affiliation) &
        political_affiliation != "Prefer not to answer" ~ "Other/Independent",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_)
  )

refs <- c(edu_4             = "High school or less",
          edu_3_top         = "High school or less",
          edu_3_mid         = "High school or less",
          education_grouped = "High school or less",
          pol_leaners_ind   = "Democrat",
          pol_strong        = "Strong Democrat",
          politics_grouped  = "Democrat")

compare_scheme <- function(v) {
  d <- alt %>% filter(!is.na(raw_milk_binary), !is.na(.data[[v]]))
  d[[v]] <- relevel(factor(d[[v]]), ref = refs[[v]])
  m     <- glm(as.formula(paste("raw_milk_binary ~", v)), data = d, family = binomial)
  m0    <- glm(raw_milk_binary ~ 1, data = d, family = binomial)
  lrt_p <- anova(m0, m, test = "LRT")$`Pr(>Chi)`[2]

  t <- alt %>%
    filter(milk_consumed %in% c("Raw dairy milk", "Both raw and pasteurized dairy milk"),
           !is.na(raw_milk_heating), !is.na(.data[[v]]))
  set.seed(2026)
  fisher_p <- fisher.test(table(t[[v]], t$raw_milk_heating),
                          simulate.p.value = TRUE, B = 10000)$p.value

  counts <- d %>% count(.data[[v]]) %>%
    mutate(txt = paste0(.data[[v]], " (", n, ")")) %>% pull(txt)

  data.frame(Scheme = v, Levels = paste(counts, collapse = "; "),
             RAny_LRT_p = round(lrt_p, 4), Thermal_Fisher_p = round(fisher_p, 4))
}

bind_rows(lapply(names(refs), compare_scheme)) %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(title = "Alternative Education and Political Orientation Codings",
             subtitle = "R_Any: likelihood ratio test vs. null; Thermal: Fisher's exact, all raw milk consumers") %>%
  cols_label(Levels = "Levels (n in R_Any sample)",
             RAny_LRT_p = "R_Any p", Thermal_Fisher_p = "Thermal p")
```

## 9. Write cleaned datasets

```{r write}
write_csv(survey_grouped, "cleaned_survey_data.csv")
write_csv(survey_base,    "survey_base_data.csv")
message("Wrote cleaned_survey_data.csv and survey_base_data.csv to: ", getwd())
```
